name: consolidation_breakout_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: A mid-session consolidation occurs when price trades in a range < 0.2% for 20+ consecutive bars after an initial directional move. This pattern represents institutional order absorption: large limit orders create a ceiling/floor, absorbing aggressive orders until the limit order is fully filled. When the consolidation breaks, the absorbed side's orders are exhausted, and the breakout direction tends to continue. This is distinct from strategy 41 (range expansion) in that this specifically looks for consolidation AFTER an initial move (continuation pattern), not a base from the session open. The edge exists because identifying real-time consolidation boundaries and distinguishing from general low-volatility drift requires specific computation.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 50 crore INR AND prior_intraday_move > 0.5% (must have moved before consolidation)

indicators.name: consol_high
indicators.params: max(high) over rolling 20 bars where range < 0.2%

indicators.name: consol_low
indicators.params: min(low) over rolling 20 bars where range < 0.2%

indicators.name: consol_duration
indicators.params: consecutive bars where price within consol_high/consol_low

conditions: prior_move_dir > 0 (consolidation after an up-move = bullish continuation pattern)
long.confirmation: close > consol_high AND (close - consol_high) > 0.05% (clear break, not marginal)

conditions: prior_move_dir < 0 (consolidation after a down-move = bearish continuation pattern)

entry.entry_price: market order on breakout bar close

exit.target: magnitude of the prior move projected from consolidation (measured move)
exit.stop_loss: opposite side of consolidation range (consol_low for longs, consol_high for shorts)
exit.trailing_stop: trail at 0.5 * consol_range_pct once profit > prior_move / 2
exit.signal_exit: exit if price closes back within consolidation for 3 bars (false breakout)

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L; tight consolidation = small stop = can size up to 1.5L

filters.volume_filter: breakout bar volume > 2x consolidation average volume
filters.trend_filter: continuation bias: long if prior move was up, short if prior move was down
filters.event_filter: skip if consolidation is due to pending news (pre-announcement quiet period)
other_filters: consolidation must be AFTER an initial 0.5%+ move — not a flat-from-open pattern (that is different)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — real-time consolidation detection with measured move targeting is a custom setup

weaknesses: Consolidation patterns can break in either direction; the prior_move_dir filter helps but continuation is not guaranteed
Very tight consolidation (0.2%) may be below the noise floor of some stocks — what looks like consolidation may be normal low-vol drift
Measured move targeting assumes symmetry (move after = move before consolidation) which is often not the case in practice
prior_art: Flag and pennant patterns are the classic continuation patterns (Edwards & Magee). The tight consolidation breakout is essentially a flag pattern quantified. Bulkowski's 'Encyclopedia of Chart Patterns' provides statistical performance of flags/pennants. The specific 0.2% range threshold and 20-bar minimum are quantitative adaptations.
notes: Edge math: 0.52 * 60bps - 0.48 * 30bps = 31.2 - 14.4 = 16.8 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ 5.8 bps per trade. Solidly positive. The tight consolidation stop (base range as stop) creates a very favorable R:R ratio. This is one of the stronger strategies due to the 2:1 winner:loser ratio. Low trade frequency (0-2/day) is the main limitation.
